bull.b: Eleven consecutive quarters of year-on-year growth indicate sustained customer adoption and expanding commercial traction rather than an isolated sales increase. Continued revenue expansion can improve operating leverage, support broader distribution, and strengthen SKYX’s position in smart home and building infrastructure.

Combining SKYX’s ceiling platform with Deako’s in-wall switches creates a broader electrical solution for builders and increases the number of products that can be sold per home. The enlarged pipeline and potential cross-selling provide a durable route to larger deployments and recurring upgrades.

Improving gross profit and a margin increase toward the low-30% range suggest that product economics remain intact as the business scales. If sustained, stronger gross margins can provide more resources for product development, distribution expansion, and eventual operating-cost absorption.

bear.b: Large and persistent operating and net losses show that revenue growth has not yet translated into sustainable profitability. The company still requires substantial cost leverage to reach break-even, making earnings durability dependent on execution, scale benefits, and successful integration of growth initiatives.

Negative operating and free cash flow indicate that the business is not currently funding its operations internally. Continued cash consumption can limit investment flexibility and increase reliance on external financing, while the absence of a specified cash-flow-positive date leaves the timing of self-funding uncertain.

The history of extremely thin equity demonstrates material balance-sheet sensitivity to losses, revaluations, and financing needs even though leverage has improved from its most stressed level. Limited equity cushioning can constrain strategic flexibility and amplify the consequences of weaker execution.
